successors.name: Principality of Hungary
successors.text: Pribina's and Kocel's land around the Zala and Lake Balaton, 'from the Rába River in the north to Pécs in the southeast and Ptuj in the west' (Pribina page); 'northwest to the Rába and Ptuj, and…

ledger.x: 838: The Franks install Pribina over Lower Pannonia.
839: 'King Louis the German had the Slavic Duchy of Lower Pannonia established in 839, ruled by ...

c. 900: 'the Frankish Empire, which lasted until the Magyar conquest (c. 900)' (Principality of Lower Pannonia page); the March of Pannonia page says only that 'by the 890s, the Pannonian March seems to have disappeared'. Braslav ruled 884-896 'under the overlordship of Arnulf of Carinthia', who handed Pannonia to him…

c. 900: The Magyars overrun the Pannonian Basin. 'Frankish domination lasted until the Magyar conquest (c. 900)'; Arnulf had handed Pannonia to Braslav in 895 or 896 to secure the frontier against the Hungarians, who had conquered Great Moravia. The Battle of Pressburg (907) follows.
c. 900: The principality ends with the Magyar conquest; no Slavic ruler is recorded after Braslav (896).

wars.name: Frankish installation of Pribina and the fall of Ratimir
wars.outcome: Ratimir of Lower Pannonia was deposed by Count Radbod (or by Ratpot, on Louis the German's orders) and Pribina installed in his place.

certainty.note: A Slavic vassal principality in forest and marsh around the Zala and Balaton; the pages name rivers and towns (Rába, Ptuj, Pécs, Zala) and no surveyed frontier.
